clue.text: He copies a kind of missile

definitions.meaning: someone who copies a drawing by going over its lines on thin paper
a bullet or shell that leaves a visible trail of light so the gunner can see its path

explanation.surface: A man reproduces the design of some sort of rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are nouns: a copyist who traces outlines, and luminous ammunition fired to show the line of fire.

clue.text: Egyptian god is evidently beginning to grow

parts.note: Ra is the sun god of ancient Egypt
taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the start of evidently is used

explanation.surface: A god of the Nile is apparently starting to get bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise crops or animals is to grow them, a common farming sense.

clue.text: Nationals are able to get short answer about aid perhaps

parts.note: can means are able

indicators.note: about places the short answer around the shuffled letters

parts.note: ANS is an abbreviation of answer

indicators.note: perhaps suggests aid in some other form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Citizens manage to give a curt reply concerning assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short answer' is the usual abbreviation, and 'about' wraps it round the rearranged aid: the A of the abbreviation comes first, the NS last.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationals are citizens of a country; people from Canada are its nationals.

clue.text: Estimating the value of a sailor

definitions.meaning: assessing or appraising the worth of something
in the Royal Navy a ... is a sailor who is not a commissioned officer

explanation.surface: Someone is putting a price on a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Appraising is assessing worth; in British naval usage an ordinary seaman below officer rank is also called this.

clue.text: Concerning currency note perhaps held by a girl

indicators.note: held by means the shuffled note goes inside the girl's name

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name

indicators.note: perhaps hints that note appears in a different form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something about money, possibly a banknote, kept by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note perhaps' looks like a banknote example; 'perhaps' instead signals the anagram, and 'held by' splits the girl's name after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Monetary describes matters of money and currency, an adjective like 'concerning currency'.

clue.text: Easy profit may be made from Poole yonder

indicators.note: may be made from signals the letters that follow are worked into a new arrangement; from is itself part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Money could be earned easily from a Dorset town over there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' looks like the link of 'made from', but its four letters are needed: FROM POOLE YONDER together give fifteen. Poole is a seaside town in Dorset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means payment for very little effort, which is what an easy profit is.

clue.text: Told the island backs Edward

indicators.note: backs means the island's name runs in the reverse direction

parts.note: Arran is an island off the west coast of Scotland
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone is told that the island supports a man named Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' reads like 'supports', but it turns ARRAN into NARRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To have narrated a story is to have recounted or related it, a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: This animal sounds lighter

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word is heard, not spelt, so the spelling changes

parts.note: a taper is a thin candle or wick used to light a fire or other candles

explanation.surface: A creature that seems less heavy than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' wants to be the comparative of light, but it is a noun: something used to light things.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapir is a hoofed mammal of the Americas and Asia with a short flexible snout.

clue.text: I'm cleared, reformed ? Exactly

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of the opening words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former wrongdoer declares himself acquitted and changed for the better, and is agreed with.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works as a whole: the anagram is signalled by 'reformed', and someone cleared and reformed has been saved from bad ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A person rescued from vice or crime, like a sinner brought back to virtue, is said to be redeemed or reclaimed.

clue.text: Quiet melody, right on pitch thanks to him

parts.note: piano is the musical direction for playing softly
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A soft tune, perfectly in key, is credited to one man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right on' looks like the slang for correct; 'right' gives R and 'on pitch' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The professional who adjusts strings makes an instrument sound in tune, so it is on pitch because of his work.

clue.text: Goodfellow gets knocked about on the ice

definitions.meaning: Robin Goodfellow, a mischievous sprite of English folklore and of A Midsummer Night's Dream

definitions.text: gets knocked about on the ice
definitions.meaning: the rubber disc struck with sticks in ice hockey

explanation.surface: A good chap is battered while skating.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Goodfellow is another name for the hobgoblin of Shakespeare's play; the same name is the hard rubber disc in ice hockey.

clue.text: Trend is for costly extremes on P.M.'s study

parts.note: the British Prime Minister lives at Number Ten Downing Street
a den is a private room for work or study

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Fashion favours lavish ends in the Prime Minister's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word placing the costly ends after the rest; the P.M. here is the British Prime Minister, whose address is Number 10.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency is an inclination or general drift, the same as a trend.

clue.text: A flier rather than a melody-maker

definitions.text: A flier rather than a melody-maker

parts.words: A flier rather than a melody-maker
parts.note: an air is a melody, so a man of airs sounds like a composer, but here the air is the sky and the man flies

explanation.surface: A pilot, as opposed to a songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot or crew member of an air force is an aviator, a flier.

clue.text: No man is an island ? Abel could have been

indicators.note: could have been suggests what the name might become if its letters were rearranged

explanation.surface: Donne's line that no man is an island, with the Biblical Abel as a counterexample.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows John Donne's 'No man is an island'; 'No man is' is just setting. Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's first exile.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is an island off the Tuscan coast of Italy.

clue.text: Most foolish at any rate

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the ... person is the most foolish
an old adverb meaning anyway or at least

explanation.surface: The silliest one, in any case.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word describes the least sensible; whole, it is an archaic adverb meaning 'at least'.

clue.text: Delivery period involving extra pay

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled from one end
time means a period

explanation.surface: Hours worked beyond the usual shift during a delivery round earn a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls (deliveries) from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment for hours beyond the normal working day is extra pay.

clue.text: Beat long-established form of wages agreement

parts.note: to thresh is to beat grain to separate it from the husks
old means long-established

explanation.surface: Defeating a traditional style of pay deal.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1970s Britain a threshold agreement gave workers automatic rises once inflation passed a set level.
explanation.definitionFit: A pay deal triggering rises when prices cross a set point was named for that trigger level.

clue.text: And language has point for a story-teller

parts.note: taken as written
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland
N, for north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A conjunction, a tongue and a full stop make a narrator.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Andersen, the Danish author of fairy tales, is a famous teller of stories.

clue.text: The lead ? Well, he chose it

definitions.text: The lead ? Well, he chose it

parts.words: The lead ? Well, he chose it
parts.note: the lead is the metal casket in The Merchant of Venice, chosen by the suitor who wins Portia

explanation.surface: Someone opts for the leading role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The lead' looks like a starring part, but it is the lead casket among gold, silver and lead in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play Portia's suitor picks the leaden casket and wins her hand.

clue.text: Measures taken to punish

definitions.meaning: a rod is an old unit of length, five and a half yards
sticks or canes used for beating offenders

explanation.surface: Steps adopted as a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Old length units and canes for beating share the name: both senses are plural nouns.

clue.text: Makes deduction in winter wear, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: dressed in furs, the warm clothing of winter

explanation.surface: A conclusion is drawn while dressed for the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce is to reach a conclusion from evidence, which is what one does in drawing an inference.

clue.text: Holy man prevailing in hostilities

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
rife means widespread or prevailing

explanation.surface: A saint is common amid warfare.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is conflict or fighting, the state of hostilities.

clue.text: Extra piece inserted 'in Borodin's étude

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An additional passage is added to a study by the Russian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a piece put into something larger, like a small map set into a corner.

clue.text: This beast is around, unhappily, no more

definitions.text: This beast is around, unhappily, no more

indicators.note: unhappily signals that the letters are in a sorry state, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creature that once roamed has sadly vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a prehistoric beast that is, sadly, no longer around.
explanation.definitionFit: The great reptiles of the Mesozoic era are extinct, so such a beast exists no more.

clue.text: Terrify a Security' Council official ?

definitions.meaning: to deprive of courage or nerve
read as two parts, a man of the United Nations, whose Security Council keeps world peace

explanation.surface: Frighten someone from the world peace body.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip of manly courage is to frighten; split, the letters name a person working for the United Nations.

clue.text: At this end one is utterly perplexed

definitions.text: At this end one is utterly perplexed

parts.words: At this end one is utterly perplexed
parts.note: refers to the idiom about being at the end of one's mental resources, totally baffled

explanation.surface: A place where a person is completely confused.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'at one's wits' end' means completely at a loss, unable to think what to do.

clue.text: Rent space in a ship-reserve supplies here

indicators.note: in places the torn space inside the ship

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
rent as a past tense means torn
room means space

explanation.surface: Hiring berth on a vessel, with spare provisions kept below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like hiring, but it is the past of rend, 'torn'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooms where reserve supplies are kept are places for storing goods.

clue.text: " My is for open war" (Milton)

parts.note: a line spoken by Moloch in Milton's Paradise Lost, with one word left out

explanation.surface: A gap in a quotation from Milton's Paradise Lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Moloch, urging war in Book II of Paradise Lost, gives his verdict: the missing word is that verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Moloch's line uses the old sense of a judgment or opinion given, a verdict in a debate.

clue.text: Not, the main way of taking part

definitions.meaning: a short railway track off the main line
taking someone's part in an argument, supporting them

explanation.surface: A minor road is a way of joining in.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway branch track off the main line, and supporting one party in a dispute, share the word.
